Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.messenger

Class P2pProtocol

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.messenger.P2pProtocol
All Implemented Interfaces:
MessengerProtocol, P2pNode.Listener
public class P2pProtocol extends Object implements MessengerProtocol, P2pNode.Listener
The native, in-process peer-to-peer backend: encrypted direct chat, presence and file transfer between LG3D nodes with no server in between, built on the reusable org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.p2p transport (X25519 + a Noise-XX-style handshake + AES-256-GCM, forward-secret and mutually authenticated). It is the second fully native backend alongside IrcProtocol; the bridge backends still hand off to external clients.

Model. A connection wraps one P2pNode: it listens for inbound peers, optionally dials the account's host:port, announces and watches for peers on the LAN, and routes each peer's frames into the Messenger's protocol-neutral ChatMessage/FileTransferEvent events. There are no channels; every peer is its own conversation, keyed by a display name derived from its nickname or identity fingerprint. sendMessage(java.lang.String, java.lang.String) accepts either a fingerprint or a display name as the target.

Trust. Identity is trust-on-first-use. An account with a pinned AccountConfig.getPeerFingerprint() accepts only that identity and refuses any other with a loud man-in-the-middle warning; an open account pins each new peer on first contact and records it in the IdentityStore. A discovered peer is only a hint to connect - its identity is always verified by the handshake, never trusted from the (spoofable) announcement.

Threading and headless-safety. The constructor is inert: it opens no socket and starts no thread. connect(org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.messenger.AccountConfig, org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.messenger.ProtocolListener) does its work on a daemon thread and reports through the ProtocolListener; every listener callback fires on a transport thread, never the Swing EDT, so the panel marshals to the EDT itself. LAN discovery degrades gracefully (it never throws) when multicast is unavailable, leaving manual host:port dialling.

Honest scope. The mesh suits 1:1 and small groups, not large-scale networks. LAN discovery is subnet-scoped; reaching a peer across the internet needs port-forwarding or a reachable host - there is no NAT hole-punching here.
